clue.text: Arthur lost at sea with frequent waves

indicators.note: being at sea means confused and all over the place, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A sailor called Arthur has gone missing on a choppy sea.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lost' reads as part of the story but its letters join Arthur's in the mix; 'at sea' alone does the stirring.
explanation.definitionFit: Radio waves of very short wavelength have a very high frequency, so ultrashort describes signals oscillating many times per second.

clue.text: Disheartened lurgy turned nasty

indicators.note: losing heart means the central letter of the following word is taken out
turned suggests the remaining letters are twisted round into a different order

blocks.note: the lurgy is British slang for an unspecified illness

explanation.surface: A bout of illness has left someone glum and in a foul mood.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing the middle R from LURGY leaves LUGY, which is rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Ugly can mean threatening or unpleasant, as in an ugly mood or an ugly situation.

clue.text: Political ideology from history is Maggie’s

indicators.note: from tells us the letters are taken out of the run of words that follows

blocks.note: the letters run across the three words

explanation.surface: Margaret Thatcher's place in history is her political creed.
explanation.walkthrough: Maggie is Margaret Thatcher, the Conservative prime minister, which makes the hidden answer especially apt.
explanation.definitionFit: Toryism is the belief system of the British Conservatives, a party political doctrine.

clue.text: Left craft area, group’s outside finished with it

indicators.note: outside says the group word wraps around the word for finished

blocks.note: A is the abbreviation for area
a band is a group, plus the possessive S
done means finished
hip means fashionable, with it

explanation.surface: A crafty group dropped out of an arts area once their work was complete.
explanation.walkthrough: Craft looks like handiwork but is a boat, and 'left' is the past tense of leave, matching the past-tense phrase.
explanation.definitionFit: To abandon ship is to leave a vessel, usually in an emergency, so the phrase means departed from a boat.

clue.text: Raising call for attention upon attack from bee

blocks.note: hoi is a shout to get someone's attention
a bee attacks with its sting

explanation.surface: Someone shouts a warning just as a bee strikes.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'upon' places the first piece on top of the second.
explanation.definitionFit: Hoisting is lifting something up, especially with ropes or a crane, so it means elevating.

clue.text: Household appliance’s beginning to be moved down list of needs

indicators.note: the first letter shifts a couple of places lower in the word, rearranging it

blocks.note: a tumble drier is a household appliance

explanation.surface: A household appliance is being moved further down someone's shopping list.
explanation.walkthrough: The D at the front of DRIER slides down two places to sit after RI.
explanation.definitionFit: A rider is a performer's list of requirements attached to a contract, such as backstage demands.

clue.text: Bringing rear forward, docks tail

indicators.note: the last letter of the word is brought round to the front

blocks.note: to dock is to cut short

explanation.surface: Moving the back end to the front, someone trims an animal's tail.
explanation.walkthrough: Dock is also what is done to a tail, which helps the disguise.
explanation.definitionFit: A scut is the short upright tail of a rabbit, hare or deer.

clue.text: Maybe blind dog following has run away

indicators.note: run away means the letter for run leaves the word before it

blocks.note: a cur is a mongrel dog
a train is a retinue, a following

explanation.surface: A guide dog's followers have bolted, perhaps leaving its owner stranded.
explanation.walkthrough: R is the cricket abbreviation for run; removing it from TRAIN leaves TAIN. 'Blind' is the window covering, not sightless.
explanation.definitionFit: A blind is one example of a window covering, and a curtain is another, hence the hedge maybe.

clue.text: Arranged ride by tram to find place that might provide deal

indicators.note: arranged means set out in a fresh order, so these letters are reordered

blocks.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone arranges a tram journey to reach a shop offering a bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: Deal is not a bargain here but softwood planks of pine or fir.
explanation.definitionFit: A timber yard sells sawn wood, and deal is a common type of softwood plank it would stock.

clue.text: Developer’s resistance to embed into soft rock

indicators.note: embedding one thing into another places it inside

blocks.note: molten rock flowing from a volcano
R is the symbol for electrical resistance

explanation.surface: A property developer faces opposition to building into soft rock.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes between the A and the V of LAVA.
explanation.definitionFit: A larva is the immature stage of an insect that will grow into the adult form, so it is still developing.

clue.text: Bad taste in house with green interior

indicators.note: interior means the green word sits inside the house word

blocks.note: taken as written
drum is British slang for a house or home
eco means environmentally friendly, green

explanation.surface: Painting the inside of a house green is a lapse in style.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests interior decor, and DECOR is indeed sitting inside the answer, though the parse splits it differently.
explanation.definitionFit: Indecorum is improper or unseemly behaviour, a lack of propriety or good manners.

clue.text: Insect made into meal for sports venue

blocks.note: a cricket is a chirping insect
grain that is ground is made into meal or flour

explanation.surface: Insects are being milled into flour to serve at a stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: Cricket is both the insect and the bat-and-ball sport, so the first piece also hints at the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A cricket ground is the field where the game of cricket is played, a type of sporting arena.

clue.text: Inconclusive list to be shortened before end

indicators.note: shortened means the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: an index is an alphabetical list
to terminate is to end

explanation.surface: An unfinished list is cut off before its conclusion.
explanation.walkthrough: INDEX loses its X; 'end' is the verb, not the noun.
explanation.definitionFit: Something indeterminate is not settled or fixed, leaving the outcome uncertain and undecided.

clue.text: Shrewd getting paid dropping off article beneath counter

indicators.note: dropping off means shedding something, here the article

blocks.note: a counter in a board game is a small disc
earning means getting paid
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A sharp shopkeeper falls asleep under the shop counter while being paid.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'beneath' puts the earning word under DISC. Counter is a game piece, not a shop counter.
explanation.definitionFit: A discerning person shows good judgement and insight, an astute and perceptive quality.

clue.text: Two of this writer’s books forthcoming

blocks.note: this writer's can be read two ways: this writer is, I'M, and belonging to this writer, MINE
NT is the New Testament, a set of books

explanation.surface: An author announces that two new books are on the way.
explanation.walkthrough: The apostrophe S does double duty: 'is' gives I'M and the possessive gives MINE.
explanation.definitionFit: Imminent means about to happen, coming very soon, close at hand.

clue.text: Almost broke case from Norway that’s thin

indicators.note: almost means not quite the whole word, so its last letter goes
the case of a word is its outside, its first and last letters

blocks.note: skint is British slang for having no money
the outside letters of Norway

explanation.surface: A nearly bankrupt traveller with a slim suitcase arrives from Norway.
explanation.walkthrough: SKINT loses its T to leave SKIN.
explanation.definitionFit: Skinny is an informal word for very slim, lean or lacking flesh.

clue.text: Briefly contemplate tramp’s recommended book

indicators.note: briefly means the word is cut short, losing its final letter

blocks.note: to muse is to contemplate
to tramp is to tread heavily; the apostrophe S is 'is', a link

explanation.surface: A vagrant briefly ponders a book someone suggested.
explanation.walkthrough: MUSE loses its E. Tramp is the verb, walk heavily, not a vagrant.
explanation.definitionFit: A must-read is a book or article so good that everyone ought to read it.

clue.text: Bug American spies used to trap rogue

indicators.note: trapping something means closing around it, so one word surrounds the other

blocks.note: the Central Intelligence Agency
a cad is a dishonourable man

explanation.surface: US intelligence plants a listening device to catch a villain.
explanation.walkthrough: With spies around, bug looks like a hidden microphone, but it is an insect.
explanation.definitionFit: A cicada is a loud chirping insect, and bug is a general word for an insect.

clue.text: Assembly company not friendly sacking six

indicators.note: sacking means dismissing, so the number word is thrown out of the friendly word

blocks.note: CO is the abbreviation for company
uncivil means rude, not friendly
VI is six in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A hostile firm's meeting ends with six people fired.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing VI from UNCIVIL leaves UNCIL.
explanation.definitionFit: A council is an elected or appointed body that meets to deliberate, a gathering of representatives.

clue.text: One buying award in possession of cavalry commander once

indicators.note: possessing something means holding it, so one word holds the other inside

blocks.note: General Custer led the US cavalry at Little Bighorn
the Order of Merit, a British honour

explanation.surface: A medal belonging to a past cavalry general is sold to a collector.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Once' marks the commander as historical: George Custer died at Little Bighorn in 1876.
explanation.definitionFit: A customer is a person who purchases goods or services from a shop or business.

clue.text: One delivers uplifting dark whiskey provided by European

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifting up means the word is read from bottom to top

blocks.note: dim means dark
W is whiskey in the NATO phonetic alphabet
if means provided that
E is the abbreviation for European

explanation.surface: A distiller ships a cheering dark whiskey made in Europe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Provided' does two jobs here: it gives IF, and 'by' joins E on the end.
explanation.definitionFit: A midwife assists women in childbirth, helping to bring babies into the world.

clue.text: Newly fitted uniform kept by salesman in case

indicators.note: kept by means held inside the word that follows

blocks.note: a rep is a sales representative
U is uniform in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a holster is a case for a gun, so holstered means put in one

explanation.surface: A travelling salesman carries his work uniform in a suitcase.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In case' looks like a phrase meaning just in case, but it is read literally as put in a holster.
explanation.definitionFit: Reupholstered furniture has been given new padding and covering fabric, refitted with fresh upholstery.

clue.text: Sign that’s plain by road regularly ignored

indicators.note: regularly ignored means every other letter is skipped, keeping the rest

blocks.note: the second, fourth, sixth, eighth and tenth letters

explanation.surface: A road sign beside a flat open plain is barely noticed.
explanation.walkthrough: Drop the first letter of the run and every second one after it.
explanation.definitionFit: Libra, the scales, is one of the twelve signs of the zodiac.

clue.text: Fish fingers, not starter

indicators.note: with no starter, the word loses its opening letter

blocks.note: to finger something is to feel it

explanation.surface: A restaurant serves fish fingers, but not as a first course.
explanation.walkthrough: Fish fingers is a dish; here 'fingers' is the verb, touches.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, so the plural noun matches the plural verb-looking definition.

clue.text: Hopelessly drunk in clubs, roll around covered in beer

indicators.note: turning around means the roll word is read backwards
covered in means wrapped inside the beer word

blocks.note: taken as written
C is the abbreviation for clubs in card games
ale is a kind of beer
a bap is a soft British bread roll

explanation.surface: A clubber, rolling around soaked in beer, is completely legless.
explanation.walkthrough: Clubs sounds like nightclubs in this boozy scene but is the card suit.
explanation.definitionFit: Incapable is used, especially in drunk and incapable, of someone too intoxicated to look after themselves.

clue.text: Wood man on horse picked up for ally

indicators.note: picked up means heard, as a radio picks up a signal

blocks.note: yew is a wood, and a knight is a man on horseback

explanation.surface: A woodsman riding a horse is collected to be someone's partner.
explanation.walkthrough: Ally here is the verb, join together.
explanation.definitionFit: To ally is to join forces, so it means combine or come together with another party.

clue.text: Metal egg uncovered, antique

indicators.note: uncovered means stripped of its outer letters on both sides

blocks.note: taken as written
antique means old

explanation.surface: An antique metal egg is unearthed, like a Faberge treasure.
explanation.walkthrough: EGG without its outer letters leaves G.
explanation.definitionFit: Gold is a precious yellow metallic element, a common example of a metal.

clue.text: Dad’s nice playing with son exuding love and sincerity

indicators.note: exuding means giving off, so that letter oozes out of the word
playing suggests the letters are moved around freely

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written
love is zero in tennis, shaped like O

explanation.surface: A father's warm game with his boy radiates affection and honesty.
explanation.walkthrough: SON loses its O to give SN, and those letters join DAD'S NICE in the mix.
explanation.definitionFit: Candidness is frankness and openness, honesty in what a person says.
